claim_source_map.passage: §2201. Emergency conservation program (a) In general The Secretary of Agriculture (referred to in this chapter as the "Secretary") is authorized to make payments to agricultural producers who carry out emergency measures to control wind erosion on farmlands or to rehabilitate farmlands damaged by wind erosion, floods, hurricanes, wildfires, or other natural disasters when, as a result of the foregoing, new conservation problems have been created that (1) if not treated, will impair or endanger the land, (2) materially affect the productive capacity of the land, (3) represent damage that is unusual in character and, except for wind erosion, is not the type that would recur frequently in the same area, and (4) will be so costly to rehabilitate that Federal assistance is or will be required to return the land to productive agricultural use. (b) Repair or replacement of fencing (1) In general With respect to a payment to an agricultural producer under subsection (a) for the repair or replacement of fencing, the Secretary shall give the agricultural producer the option of receiving not more than 25 percent of the payment, determined by the Secretary based on the applicable percentage of the fair market value of the cost of the repair or replacement, before the agricultural producer carries out the repair or replacement. (2) Return of funds If the funds provided under paragraph (1) are not expended by the end of the 60-day period beginning on the date on which the agricultural producer receives those funds, the funds shall be returned within a reasonable timeframe, as determined by the Secretary.

claim_source_map.passage: §2206. Emergency forest restoration program (a) Definitions In this section: (1) Emergency measures The term "emergency measures" means those measures that— (A) are necessary to address damage caused by a natural disaster to natural resources on nonindustrial private forest land, and the damage, if not treated— (i) would impair or endanger the natural resources on the land; and (ii) would materially affect future use of the land; and (B) would restore forest health and forest-related resources on the land. (2) Natural disaster The term "natural disaster" includes wildfires, hurricanes or excessive winds, drought, ice storms or blizzards, floods, or other resource-impacting events, as determined by the Secretary. (3) Nonindustrial private forest land The term "nonindustrial private forest land" means rural land, as determined by the Secretary, that— (A) has existing tree cover (or had tree cover immediately before the natural disaster and is suitable for growing trees); and (B) is owned by any nonindustrial private individual, group, association, corporation, or other private legal entity, that has definitive decision-making authority over the land. (b) Availability of assistance The Secretary may make payments to an owner of nonindustrial private forest land who carries out emergency measures to restore the land after the land is damaged by a natural disaster. (c) Eligibility To be eligible to receive a payment under subsection (b), an owner must demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Secretary that the nonindustrial private forest land on which the emergency measures are carried out had tree cover immediately before the natural disaster. (d) Cost share requirement Payments made under subsection (b) shall not exceed 75 percent of the total cost of the emergency measures carried out by an owner of nonindustrial private forest land. (e) Authorization of appropriations There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary such funds as may be necessary to carry out this section. Amounts so appropriated shall remain available until expended.

(a) In General.--Beginning on the date that is 270 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, an employee of the Administration that will personally and substantially participate in the origination, review, or approval of a loan administered by the Administration shall, prior to such participation in such loan, certify to the Administrator in writing that such employee-- (1) to their knowledge, does not have any conflict of interest prohibited under section 208 of title 18, United States Code, or section 2635.502 of title 5, Code of Federal Regulations, with respect to such participation in such loan; (2) upon learning of any such conflict of interest after submitting such certification, will immediately disclose such conflict of interest to the supervisor of such employee and recuse themselves from participating in such loan; and (3) understands the requirements applicable to such employee under Federal law and regulations of the Administration regarding conflicts of interest with respect to such participation in such loan. action.short_description: Changing conservation restoration advances and wildfire categories
action.compact_description: S.629 would broaden qualified conservation advances:75percent of replacement cost and50percent of repair/restoration cost, with a180day unspent predicate. A separate forest advance is capped at75percent of cost; the existing total assistance cap remains. Federal-caused fire is separately listed. Whole-program Infrastructure membership remains unaccepted.
action.meaning:
The House passed the motion to suspend the rules and pass S.629 in the retained Senate-engrossed version. That chamber action does not itself enact the bill or deliver assistance. The whole choice amends the existing emergency conservation and private-forest restoration programs, not a new general disaster entitlement.
For emergency conservation, the existing2201(a) predicates remain: qualifying emergency erosion control or disaster-damaged farmland rehabilitation, new conservation problems that threaten land, materially affect productive capacity, are unusual/nonfrequent subject to the wind-erosion distinction, and are sufficiently costly to require Federal assistance. The bill extends the existing fencing advance option to other emergency measures to replace or restore farmland or conservation structures requiring an immediate response as determined by the Secretary. Before the work, the Secretary shall give the producer the option of receiving75percent of replacement COST or50percent of repair/restoration COST, each as determined by the Secretary. These are the printed percentages of COST, not caps expressed as percentages of payment and not the earlier H.R.1011 wording. The existing unspent-funds predicate changes from60days to180days after receipt; return remains within a reasonable timeframe determined by the Secretary, not necessarily on day180 itself.
New2201(c) lists two wildfire categories: a nonnatural wildfire IF damage is caused by its spread due to natural causes, AND a separately listed Federal-caused wildfire. The natural-spread condition is printed in the first item, not imposed on the separate Federal-caused item. This does not establish actual Federal fault, automatically approve a claimant, or erase subsection(a)'s remaining predicates. The2206(a)(2) definition similarly includes nonnatural fire with the natural-spread damage condition and Federal-caused wildfire as distinct included categories, within the existing natural-disaster definition.
For emergency forest restoration, the Secretary shall give the eligible nonindustrial private forest owner an option before emergency measures of receiving NOT MORE THAN75percent of their COST, determined by the Secretary. This advance cap is separate from the retained75percent total-cost assistance cap in2206(d). Rural/private land and tree-cover predicates, Secretary determinations and the existing discretionary payment authority remain; the bill does not guarantee every owner assistance. Unspent advance funds after180days from receipt must be returned within a reasonable Secretary-determined timeframe. The existing such-sums authorization is redesignated, with no fixed new appropriation supplied by this bill. Individual eligibility, State technical standards, funding availability and current consolidated implementation are not certified.
A Yea supports this whole suspension/passage choice; a Nay opposes it without identifying a preferred component or alternative. Infrastructure/Technology membership is an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal based on physical farmland/conservation-structure and forest rehabilitation, coupled with qualified advance assistance. A competing boundary treats the whole package as private agricultural/forestry disaster assistance. Independent whole-version, baseline and taxonomy review is required. No realized restoration, payment, environmental benefit, motive or enactment is inferred.
limitations: Distinct S.629 wording: ECP exact75/50percent of COST, not H.R.1011 payment-base caps.
180day unspent predicate and reasonable Secretary return timeframe are distinct; remaining farmland eligibility persists.
Nonnatural natural-spread category and separately listed Federal-caused category are not collapsed; no actual fault or automatic approval.
Forest advance cap and existing75percent total-cost cap are separate; rural/private/tree-cover eligibility retained.
No fixed new appropriation, individual eligibility, technical-standard implementation or realized outcome certified.
Whole physical rehabilitation versus agricultural/forestry assistance taxonomy remains unaccepted.

Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled, SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE. This Act may be cited as the ``Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act of 2025''. SEC. 2. IMPROVING THE EMERGENCY CONSERVATION PROGRAM. Section 401 of the Agricultural Credit Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2201) is amended-- (1) in subsection (b)-- (A) in the subsection heading, by inserting ``and Other Emergency Conservation Measures'' after ``Fencing''; (B) in paragraph (1)-- (i) by inserting ``or for other emergency measures to replace or restore farmland or conservation structures requiring an immediate response (as determined by the Secretary),'' after ``replacement of fencing,''; and (ii) by striking ``option of receiving'' and all that follows through the period at the end and inserting the following: ``option of receiving, before the agricultural producer carries out the repair, replacement, or restoration-- ``(A) with respect to a payment to the agricultural producer for a replacement, 75 percent of the cost of the replacement, as determined by the Secretary; and ``(B) with respect to a payment to the agricultural producer for a repair or restoration, 50 percent of the cost of the repair or restoration, as determined by the Secretary.''; and (C) in paragraph (2), by striking ``60-day'' and inserting ``180-day''; and (2) by adding at the end the following: ``(c) Wildfire Determination.--A wildfire that causes damage eligible for a payment under subsection (a) includes-- ``(1) a wildfire that is not caused naturally, if the damage is caused by the spread of the wildfire due to natural causes; and ``(2) a wildfire that is caused by the Federal Government.''. SEC. 3. IMPROVING THE EMERGENCY FOREST RESTORATION PROGRAM. Section 407 of the Agricultural Credit Act of 1978 (16 U.S.C. 2206) is amended-- (1) in subsection (a)(2), by striking ``wildfires,'' and inserting ``wildfires (including a wildfire that is not caused naturally, if the damage is caused by the spread of the wildfire due to natural causes, and a wildfire that is caused by the Federal Government),''; (2) by redesignating subsection (e) as subsection (f); and (3) by inserting after subsection (d) the following: ``(e) Advance Payments.-- ``(1) In general.--The Secretary shall give an owner of nonindustrial private forest land the option of receiving, before the owner carries out emergency measures under this section, not more than 75 percent of the cost of the emergency measures, as determined by the Secretary. ``(2) Return of funds.--If the funds provided under paragraph (1) are not expended by the end of the 180-day period beginning on the date on which the owner of nonindustrial private forest land receives those funds, the funds shall be returned within a reasonable timeframe, as determined by the Secretary.''. Passed the Senate March 24, 2026. claim_source_map.passage: §2201. Emergency conservation program (a) In general The Secretary of Agriculture (referred to in this chapter as the "Secretary") is authorized to make payments to agricultural producers who carry out emergency measures to control wind erosion on farmlands or to rehabilitate farmlands damaged by wind erosion, floods, hurricanes, wildfires, or other natural disasters when, as a result of the foregoing, new conservation problems have been created that (1) if not treated, will impair or endanger the land, (2) materially affect the productive capacity of the land, (3) represent damage that is unusual in character and, except for wind erosion, is not the type that would recur frequently in the same area, and (4) will be so costly to rehabilitate that Federal assistance is or will be required to return the land to productive agricultural use. (b) Repair or replacement of fencing (1) In general With respect to a payment to an agricultural producer under subsection (a) for the repair or replacement of fencing, the Secretary shall give the agricultural producer the option of receiving not more than 25 percent of the payment, determined by the Secretary based on the applicable percentage of the fair market value of the cost of the repair or replacement, before the agricultural producer carries out the repair or replacement. (2) Return of funds If the funds provided under paragraph (1) are not expended by the end of the 60-day period beginning on the date on which the agricultural producer receives those funds, the funds shall be returned within a reasonable timeframe, as determined by the Secretary.

claim_source_map.passage: §2206. Emergency forest restoration program (a) Definitions In this section: (1) Emergency measures The term "emergency measures" means those measures that— (A) are necessary to address damage caused by a natural disaster to natural resources on nonindustrial private forest land, and the damage, if not treated— (i) would impair or endanger the natural resources on the land; and (ii) would materially affect future use of the land; and (B) would restore forest health and forest-related resources on the land. (2) Natural disaster The term "natural disaster" includes wildfires, hurricanes or excessive winds, drought, ice storms or blizzards, floods, or other resource-impacting events, as determined by the Secretary. (3) Nonindustrial private forest land The term "nonindustrial private forest land" means rural land, as determined by the Secretary, that— (A) has existing tree cover (or had tree cover immediately before the natural disaster and is suitable for growing trees); and (B) is owned by any nonindustrial private individual, group, association, corporation, or other private legal entity, that has definitive decision-making authority over the land. (b) Availability of assistance The Secretary may make payments to an owner of nonindustrial private forest land who carries out emergency measures to restore the land after the land is damaged by a natural disaster. (c) Eligibility To be eligible to receive a payment under subsection (b), an owner must demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Secretary that the nonindustrial private forest land on which the emergency measures are carried out had tree cover immediately before the natural disaster. (d) Cost share requirement Payments made under subsection (b) shall not exceed 75 percent of the total cost of the emergency measures carried out by an owner of nonindustrial private forest land. (e) Authorization of appropriations There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary such funds as may be necessary to carry out this section. Amounts so appropriated shall remain available until expended.

action.short_description: Clarifying business loans for software, cloud services and AI tools
action.compact_description: The bill would expressly permit discretionary7(a) loans for specified business software/cloud/technology uses, including AI tools. It does not imply earlier loans were forbidden, authorize R&D use or narrow working capital. It supplies no fixed appropriation or automatic loan approval. Whole credit-versus-technology membership remains unaccepted.
action.meaning:
The House passed suspension and H.R.915 as amended in the retained House-engrossed version. That vote does not itself enact the bill, approve a loan or require software adoption. The whole bill adds paragraph38to the existing7(a) business-loan authority, with three express construction limits.
The Administration MAY provide loans under7(a), in whole or in part, for business software, cloud computing services or such technology facilitating business operations, product/service delivery, payroll processing/payment/tracking, human resources, sales/billing, or accounting/tracking supplies, inventory, records and expenses. Included business tools may utilize artificial intelligence. It is discretionary loan authority, not an AI grant, compulsory purchase or automatic approval for every business.
The bill expressly does NOT imply that pre-enactment7(a) loans for these purposes were impermissible. It does NOT authorize research-and-development use and does NOT limit the definition of working capital. Existing allowable uses are clarified; this is not proof that all listed software financing was previously prohibited. The retained636(a) opening already empowers loans for qualified small businesses, including working capital, to the extent and amounts provided in advance in appropriation Acts, directly or through participating financial institutions. That opening does not establish the remainder of7(a)'s restrictions, individual eligibility, current guarantee terms, rates or caps; none is newly invented here. The separately retained636(b) disaster-loan unit is not the operative7(a) baseline and is not used to impose disaster predicates on these loans. No fixed new appropriation or loan amount is supplied by H.R.915.
A Yea supports this whole software/cloud/technology loan-use clarification with all three construction limits; a Nay opposes it without a component-specific position. Infrastructure/Technology membership is an UNACCEPTED candidate proposal based on explicit business software/cloud/AI access within the whole loan-use bill. A competing boundary treats the package as ordinary small-business credit policy. Independent baseline, whole-version and taxonomy review is required. No actual loan, adoption, improved productivity, AI safety result, motive or enactment is inferred.
limitations: Discretionary7(a) loan-use clarification, not an AI grant, mandate or automatic approval.
Three construction limits preserve prior permissibility, do not authorize R&D and do not narrow working capital.
Only636(a) opening retained; remaining restrictions/current eligibility/guarantee terms/rates/caps not certified.
636(b) disaster predicates are not imported into7(a).
No fixed new appropriation, individual loan, adoption or realized benefit; whole credit-versus-technology taxonomy unaccepted.
